title: Functional Adoption Index (FAI) — Scoring Worksheet and Runbook
body:
Purpose:
This working doc defines the Functional Adoption Index (FAI): a composite health score focused on product functionality usage (not just login or session counts). FAI is intended to surface accounts that are at risk because customers are not adopting key features that correlate with renewal and expansion.

Summary / Why FAI is different:
- Many existing health scores lean heavily on volume (api calls, sessions). FAI emphasizes functional depth and successful task completion.
- Designed to be lightweight to compute from product analytics + support CRM events, and actionable (maps to a 3-tier response playbook).

High-level components (suggested):
1) Core Task Completion Rate (CTR) — % of scheduled primary workflows successfully completed in a 30d window (weight 30%).
2) Feature Breadth (FB) — fraction of recommended product modules used at least once in 30d (weight 20%).
3) Feature Depth (FD) — median number of distinct advanced actions per active user (weight 15%).
4) Time to First Success (TFS) — days from sign-up/onboarding to first successful run of the primary workflow (normalized, lower is better) (weight 15%).
5) Support Friction Index (SFI) — normalized count of active support tickets + repeat errors per 30d (weight 10%, negative contributor).
6) Automation / Integration Adoption (AIA) — presence and recency of integrations, scheduled jobs, or API keys being used (weight 10%).

Scoring formula (normalized 0-100):
- Normalize each component to 0-100 using historical percentiles (recommended: 5th-95th mapping to 0-100 to reduce outliers).
- FAI = 0.30*CTR + 0.20*FB + 0.15*FD + 0.15*(100 - TFS_norm) + 0.10*(100 - SFI_norm) + 0.10*AIA
- Example: CTR=80, FB=60, FD=40, TFS_norm=30, SFI_norm=20, AIA=50 => FAI = 0.3*80+0.2*60+0.15*40+0.15*(70)+0.1*(80)+0.1*50 = 24+12+6+10.5+8+5 = 65.5

Thresholds & risk tiers (suggested):
- Healthy (FAI >= 75): low-touch, standard renewal cadence 
- Watch (55 <= FAI < 75): proactive engagement, enablement nudges, technical check 
- At-risk (35 <= FAI < 55): immediate CS outreach, product fixes prioritized, success plan 
- Critical (FAI < 35): escalation to Customer Success Manager + Solutions Eng, possible executive touch and discount risk

Signal definitions and data queries (examples to provide to analytics):
- CTR: count(successful_primary_workflow) / count(expected_primary_workflow_opportunities) over 30d. SQL hint: group by account_id, metric_date windowed.
- FB: count(distinct module_id where last_used_date >= now()-30d) / count(recommended_modules_for_segment).
- FD: median(distinct advanced_action_types per user) among users who performed primary workflow at least once in 30d.
- TFS_norm: compute days from first_login -> first_success, cap at 90d, map to percentile scale.
- SFI: weight support tickets by severity (sev1=3, sev2=2, sev3=1) + distinct error-class occurrences identified in telemetry.
- AIA: binary 0/100 score: 100 if integration or API key active in last 30d, 0 otherwise; consider gradation for scheduled jobs frequency.

Sample worksheet (copy into sheet, rows = accounts):
Columns: account_id, plan_tier, ARR, primary_ctr_30d, feature_breadth_30d, feature_depth_median, tfs_days, sfi_norm, aia_score, fai_score, risk_tier, last_success_date, last_support_ticket, owner, next_action
Example row (text):
acct_0234, pro, 120000, 0.78, 0.6, 3, 5, 0.15, 0.60, Watch, 2025-05-18, TKT-924, Maya S., "Trigger onboarding webinar invite; run telemetry sanity check"

Playbook mapping (actions per tier) — explicit steps to make operational:
- Healthy: monthly health digest; automated tips email; include in upsell cadence. Ownership: CSM (light).
- Watch: schedule 30-minute enablement session; share 3 success plays; check feature flags and integration logs. Ownership: CSM + Solutions Engineer (optional). Template subject: "Quick wins we see for <use-case> at <account>".
- At-risk: run diagnostic checklist (see appendix), open product bug ticket if telemetry indicates recurring errors, propose targeted workshop (1-2 weeks). Offer case studies and tailored success metrics. Ownership: Senior CSM + SE. Escalation: ask for AM/RevOps review. Template subject: "Action plan to stabilize product usage at <account>".
- Critical: mobilize emergency task force; propose on-site or virtual deep-dive; prepare contract/renewal risk brief for GTM leadership. Ownership: CSM Lead, Solutions Eng, AE, Customer Support Manager. Template subject: "Urgent: proposed recovery plan for <account> — timeline & resources required".

Diagnostic checklist (for At-risk and Critical):
- Verify data fidelity: event ingestion delays? Are primary workflow success events reliable?
- Reproduce failure: ask engineering to reproduce error with reproducible steps.
- Check onboarding flow: was a critical step skipped? Are training materials out of date?
- Integration health: are webhooks/API responses returning 4xx/5xx?
- Permission or seat issues: are users blocked by roles?
- Quota or rate-limit throttling: check infra logs for throttling incidents.

Quick SQL snippets (analytics team):
- CTR: SELECT account_id, sum(case when event='primary_success' then 1 else 0 end)::float / nullif(sum(case when event in ('primary_attempt','primary_success') then 1 else 0 end),0) AS ctr_30d FROM events WHERE event_time >= now()- interval '30 days' GROUP BY account_id;
- FB: SELECT account_id, count(distinct module_id) / <recommended_count> AS fb_30d FROM module_usage WHERE last_used >= now()- interval '30 days' GROUP BY account_id;

Owner playbook snippets (customer messaging examples):
- Watch outreach (email snippet): "Hi <Name> — noticed your team has been using <feature A> but not <feature B>, which often unlocks 30% more value. Would you be open to a quick 20-minute walk-through next week?"
- At-risk outreach (email snippet): "Hi <Name> — we saw repeated errors impacting your workflows and want to prioritize a fix. Can we schedule a workshop to align on root cause and a recovery plan? Our team will run diagnostics in parallel"

Operational notes and governance:
- Update cadence: recompute FAI nightly. Re-evaluate component weights quarterly based on correlation with renewal/expansion outcomes.
- Data ownership: analytics to maintain queries, product telemetry to own event contracts, CS to annotate manual edge-cases in the sheet.
- Privacy: ensure PII stripped from event pipelines used for scoring; only store account-level rollups in the sheet.

Open questions / next steps (working list):
- Should SFI be negative in formula (we subtract its normalized score) or flipped earlier for clarity? Proposal: keep as negative contributor to make FAI intuitive (higher = better).
- How to handle seasonal customers with bursty usage patterns (e.g., monthly jobs)? Proposal: add a burst-adjustment factor for scheduled usage profiles.
- Which recommended_modules_for_segment should be authoritative: product-configured or sales-mapped? Action: sync with product to publish canonical lists.
- Implementation owner: analytics + CS ops. Timeline: prototype (queries + sheet) in 2 sprints, pilot on 50 accounts, iterate.

Appendix (diagnostic checklist details, ownership matrix, sample JIRA templates, SQL snippets) — keep in Confluence linked artifact for full version.

Notes to reviewers (quick ask):
- Please comment on the weights and the TFS normalizer choice.
- If you have recent correlation analysis (FAI components -> churn/renewal), attach link in comments.

Last edited by Priya Nair on 2025-06-20. Document is intentionally written as a working worksheet — expect tweaks and simpler formula variants during pilot.
